note.text:
In 1803–1808 the English chemist John Dalton proposed his atomic theory:
1. All matter is made of very small particles called atoms.
2. Atoms cannot be divided, created or destroyed.
3. All the atoms of one element are identical (same mass, same properties); atoms of different elements are different.
4. Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds (water: two hydrogen atoms to one oxygen atom).
5. In a chemical reaction atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed.
Later discoveries changed two points: atoms CAN be divided (into protons, neutrons and electrons), and atoms of one element can have different masses (isotopes).

worked_example.problem: Use Dalton's theory to explain what happens to the atoms when hydrogen burns in oxygen to make {e}.
steps: The hydrogen and oxygen atoms are not destroyed and no new atoms are made.
They are rearranged: they join in a simple whole-number ratio, two hydrogen atoms to one oxygen atom.
worked_example.answer: The atoms are rearranged into {e}, in the ratio two H to one O; none is created or destroyed.

cards.idea: Dalton said that all matter is made of tiny atoms that cannot be divided, created or destroyed.
example: A grain of salt contains a huge number of atoms.
In a reaction the atoms are only rearranged.

cards.idea: Atoms of one element are all alike; atoms of different elements are different. Atoms join in simple whole-number ratios.
example: All carbon atoms are carbon atoms.
Water: two H atoms to one O atom.

cards.idea: Two of Dalton's ideas were later changed: atoms can be divided, and atoms of one element can have different masses.
example: Atoms contain protons, neutrons and electrons.
Atoms of one element with different masses are isotopes.

pick.q: Which of Dalton's ideas is no longer accepted?
pick.y: Atoms are made of smaller particles.

pick.q: What are atoms of one element with different masses called?
pick.y: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

questions.prompt: Which statement is part of Dalton's atomic theory?

right.text: All matter is made of tiny particles called atoms.
Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds.
In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged.
Atoms of different elements are different.

wrong.text: Atoms are made of protons, neutrons and electrons.
wrong.explain: That was discovered later; Dalton thought atoms could not be divided.

wrong.text: Matter is a continuous substance with no particles.
wrong.explain: Dalton said matter is made of atoms.

wrong.text: New atoms are created in every reaction.
wrong.explain: Dalton said atoms are not created or destroyed.

pick.q: Water has two hydrogen atoms for every oxygen atom. Which idea of Dalton does this show?
pick.r: Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios.
e: Dalton said they cannot be divided.
Dalton said they are not destroyed.
pick.y: Two to one is a simple whole-number ratio.

pick.q: Who proposed the atomic theory in the early 1800s?
e: Newton worked on forces and motion.
Mendeleev made the periodic table later.

pick.q: According to Dalton, what happens to atoms in a chemical reaction?
e: Dalton said atoms are not destroyed.
Dalton said atoms are not created.

pick.q: Which of Dalton's ideas is no longer accepted?
pick.y: Atoms are made of smaller particles.

pick.q: What are atoms of one element with different masses called?
pick.y: Isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

questions.prompt: Which statement does NOT agree with Dalton's theory?

right.text: Atoms of one element are identical.
Atoms are not destroyed in reactions.

wrong.text: Half an atom of oxygen joins with one atom of hydrogen.
wrong.explain: Dalton said atoms join in whole-number ratios; atoms cannot be split.
Dalton said atoms are rearranged, not destroyed.

wrong.text: Atoms of copper and gold are identical.
wrong.explain: Atoms of different elements are different.
